app/src/routes/moves/[name].js:58,69 — Map→Object→Map typeNames serialization repeated at every route boundary

coupling.rationale: Routes depend on narrow, well-factored lib seams and server/client code is cleanly separated; the prop-serialization friction and the media-URL pattern living in views.js are tangles, not knots.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.js:56-78 — pokemonRefsToSpecies with extraOf callback: one abstraction covers moves, abilities and type pages including alt-form exclusion and ordering
app/src/lib/views.js:15-17 — pokemonCard options.types/options.note model real variation instead of flag parameters
app/src/routes/index.js:149 — cardList(...map(pokemonCard...)) expression duplicated in four routes rather than a shared list helper
app/src/routes/moves/[name].js:35-38 — 404/document wiring boilerplate copied into four route files
abstraction_design.rationale: The core abstractions (species resolution, cards, formatters) stretch to new cases well; small scaffolding (option(), not-found blocks, typeNames dance) is copy-pasted across routes, so cross-cutting list changes touch every route.

findings.issue: Card sprites are constructed from a hardcoded media-URL pattern keyed by species ID instead of using the default Pokémon's sprites.front_default, which breaks for any species whose default form's sprite URL deviates and ignores data already fetched in pokemonRefsToSpecies (app/src/lib/data.js:60-70)
findings.suggestion: Capture pokemon.sprites?.front_default in pokemonRefsToSpecies and have pokemonCard prefer it, falling back to spriteUrl only for the home list

findings.issue: The card-list rendering expression is duplicated in four routes (also routes/moves/[name].js:118, routes/abilities/[name].js:83, routes/types/[name].js:84), so cross-cutting changes like sorting touch every route
findings.suggestion: Extract a pokemonCards(species, typeNames, opts) helper in views.js and route all four call sites through it

findings.issue: The route handler is ~330 lines mixing summary, stats, abilities, evolution and version-group/moves logic, making targeted edits harder
findings.suggestion: Extract pure data-prep helpers (e.g. buildMovesTables, buildVersionGroups) into lib/data.js or a local module

findings.issue: typeNames Map→Object→Map serialization dance duplicated in all five routes
findings.suggestion: Add toPlain/toMap helpers in util.js, or pass a lookup function instead of a serialized map

findings.issue: The 404 status/props plus document title wiring block is copied in four route files
findings.suggestion: A small withNotFound(document) wrapper in views.js would remove the copy-paste when adding new resource pages

findings.issue: The fetch/DOMParser/replaceWith refresh helper is near-identical in routes/pokemon/[name].client.js:12
findings.suggestion: Move the swap-in-fragment-by-id helper into a shared client util imported by both scripts

findings.issue: option() select-option helper defined twice (also routes/index.js:15)

findings.suggestion: Remove it from the import list

summary: This is an easy codebase to own: the lib layer gives every route narrow fetch/cache, species-resolution and card-render seams, so removing a feature is a directory delete plus one section edit and changing the data source touches exactly one file. The main editability costs are duplicated route scaffolding (option helper, 404 blocks, typeNames serialization, client refresh) and card sprites built from a URL pattern instead of the API-provided URL, which forces a two-file fix for the Deoxys-class sprite bug. The 330-line Pokémon route handler concentrates five concerns in one place, slightly raising the cost of targeted edits there.
